en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 13.12.
Parittattika (The Triplet on the Limited)
Dependent on a limited state by way of root condition, a non-limited state arises. Dependent on a limited state by way of root condition, a non-exalted state arises.
Dependent on a limited state by way of root condition, a non-infinite state arises.
A state arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a limited state, states that are neither limited nor immeasurable arise by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a limited state, states that are neither exalted nor immeasurable arise by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a sublime state, a non-sublime state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a sublime state, a limited state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a sublime state, an immeasurable state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a sublime state, a state that is neither limited nor immeasurable...
And states arise conditioned by a cause. Dependent on a sublime state, both non-sublime and non-immeasurable states arise conditioned by a cause.
Dependent on an immeasurable state, a non-immeasurable state arises conditioned by a cause. Dependent on an immeasurable state...
Dependent on a limited state, a state that is neither limited nor sublime arises by way of the root condition.

Dependent on an immeasurable state, a state that is not sublime arises by way of the root condition. Dependent on an immeasurable state, states that are neither sublime nor immeasurable arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on an immeasurable state, states that are neither limited nor sublime... [arise] by way of the root condition.
And states arise by way of root-condition.
Dependent on limited and immeasurable states, a non-exalted state arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on limited and immeasurable states, a non-immeasurable state arises by way of root-condition. Limited and...
Conditioned by an immeasurable state, limited and sublime states arise by way of root-condition.
Conditioned by both limited and sublime states, a non-limited state arises by way of root-condition.
Conditioned by both limited and sublime states, a non-sublime state arises by way of root-condition. Conditioned by both limited and...
Dependent on a sublime state, a non-infinite state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both limited and sublime states, neither-limited-nor-infinite states arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on both limited and sublime states, neither-sublime-nor-infinite states arise.
By way of root condition. (Abbreviated.

Under root there are twenty-three; under object, fourteen; under predominance, nineteen … pe … under mutuality, sixteen … pe … under prenascence and repetition, nine … pe … under non-disappearance, twenty-three. (The full detail should be expanded in all cases.)
